pages.title: Orders Service Architecture
pages.excerpt: Overview of the orders service components and request flow.
pages.body:
Architecture

The FastAPI API receives orders, reserves stock in Redis and stores orders in Postgres. A Celery worker sends email notifications. Payments are processed by Stripe.

pages.title: Payments Runbook
pages.excerpt: What to do when payments fail, double charges or refunds go wrong.
pages.body: Duplicate charges: check the idempotency key in the payment service logs. Refunds: partial refunds are issued from the refund service. Webhook failures: confirm the Stripe webhook secret.

pages.title: Authentication and Session Policy
pages.excerpt: How login, JWT access tokens and refresh tokens work.
pages.body: Access tokens are JWTs valid for 15 minutes. Clients call the refresh endpoint to get a new token. Passwords are verified on login.

pages.title: Deployment Process
pages.body: CI builds a Docker image, pushes to ECR and updates the ECS service. Alembic migrations run before rollout. Rollback by redeploying the previous image.

pages.title: Database Schema and Migrations
pages.excerpt: Tables in the orders database and how to change them.
pages.body: Tables: customers, orders, order_items. Orders reference customers. Schema changes use Alembic migrations.

pages.title: Email Notifications Design
pages.body: Emails are sent by a Celery task. Failed sends are retried every 60 seconds up to 5 times.

pages.title: API Rate Limiting Policy
pages.excerpt: Request limits for public API clients.
pages.body: Each client IP may make 60 requests per minute. Over the limit the API returns 429.

pages.title: Team Onboarding
pages.excerpt: Start here if you are new to the team.
pages.body: Install tools, request access and read the architecture page.
